title: Polynomial-fraction generators span the actual differential fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $x\in X$, $W\subseteq X$ open containing $x$, $I$ any index set, and $a_j\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$ for $j\in I$. Write $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $\rho:k\to R$ for the structure map, $c_j$ for the germ of $a_j$, and $K=\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Assume that for every $t\in R$ there exist $p,q\in k[Z_j\mid j\in I]$ such that $q(c)$ is a unit in $R$ and $tq(c)=p(c)$, with polynomial constants evaluated by $\rho$. Then the elements $1\otimes d(c_j)$ span the actual fibre $K\otimes_R(\Omega^1_{X/k})_x$ over $K$ [def-weil-module-base-change; def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf; lem-pur-conormal-sequence-smooth-immersion]. Equivalently, the actual differential germs of the $a_j$, in relativeDifferentialsStalkFibre f (id X) x, span that fibre. No smoothness, immersion, finiteness of I, or rationality of x is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00RM, section-differentials: definition-derivation and the free-module presentation of Omega; Tag 00RT, lemma-differentials-localize, quotient-rule proof. The scheme differential sheaf is Constructions Tag 01UM.

proof.text: Use the proved fieldDifferentialsSelfFibreEquiv and its germ formula from ConormalSequenceSmoothImmersion to identify the actual differential fibre with K tensor_R Omega_(R/k), sending each differential germ to 1 tensor D(c_j). This uses only the universal-derivation stalk comparison, not the smooth conormal short exact sequence.

Let P be the K-span of 1 tensor D(c_j) and delta:Omega_(R/k) -> K tensor_R Omega_(R/k) be m -> 1 tensor m. Induct on polynomials using the constant, sum and multiplication-by-variable constructors. Constants have zero derivative. Additivity and Leibniz, followed by R-linearity of delta, show delta(D(p(c))) belongs to P for every polynomial p. Restricting scalars of P permits multiplication by any element of R.

For a in R choose a*q(c)=p(c) with q(c) a unit. Differentiate to obtain q(c) delta(D(a))=delta(D(p(c)))-a delta(D(q(c))). The right side lies in P by the preceding induction. Multiply by the R-unit inverse of q(c), so delta(D(a)) lies in P for every a. Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.span_range_derivation and span induction imply delta(m) lies in P for every differential m. Tensor induction finishes: every pure tensor b tensor m equals b times delta(m), and sums stay in P. Thus P is the whole tensor module. Transport the equality of spans back along the germ-preserving equivalence.

lean.statement:
theorem span_differentialFibreGerm_of_localFractions
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    (x : X) (W : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ W) {I : Type v} (a : I → Γ(X, W))
    (hfrac : let ρ : k →+* X.presheaf.stalk x :=
        ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom
      let c : I → X.presheaf.stalk x := fun j ↦ X.presheaf.germ W x hx (a j)
      ∀ t : X.presheaf.stalk x, ∃ p q : MvPolynomial I k,
        IsUnit (MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ρ c q) ∧
        t * MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ρ c q = MvPolynomial.eval₂Hom ρ c p) :
    Submodule.span (X.residueField x) (Set.range fun j ↦
      relativeDifferentialsStalkFibreGerm f (𝟙 X) x W hx (a j)) = ⊤
